display.purpose: Hero name only. One per site.

headline.purpose: Deep-dive page h1 and story-act eyebrows. One per page.

title.purpose: Card titles, drawer headings, section headings.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy. Cap at 65–75ch on prose pages.

body-small.purpose: Card summaries, meta rows, button labels, drawer body. The dominant scale.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, tag-type headers, taxonomy sublabels. Uppercase, tracked +0.25em.

shadows.name: card-hover-glow
shadows.purpose: The single shadow in the system. Appears only on Experience Card hover, paired with a -2px Y translate. The lamp's reflection on the workbench.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Color transitions, hover state shifts on buttons, pills, links.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Theme cross-fade on <html>, card hover lift, navbar scroll transition.

motion.name: ease-out-quint
motion.purpose: Default reveal easing. Starts fast, settles slow — quiet but deliberate.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Color/hover transitions where the eased exit isn't load-bearing.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Animation + transition duration override under prefers-reduced-motion. The end state renders immediately.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Drawer flips from bottom-sheet to right slide-over; navbar shows desktop links.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Grid moves to 2 columns; ambient hero typography scales up.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Grid moves to 3 columns; deep-dive page becomes two-column with sticky sidebar; story timeline becomes alternating centre rail.

components.name: Tag Pill — Muted
components.description: Tag chip rendered when a filter is active and this slug doesn't match. The 'here's why this entry isn't a primary hit' state.
components.css: .ds-tag-pill--muted { color: var(--color-text-muted); border-color: var(--color-border); background: transparent; }

narrative.overview: The site is a workshop with the lights on at evening. A dark, considered interior where the work is laid out plainly, and one warm lamp — the Ember Sunset accent — marks where the visitor's hand should go next. Nothing performs. Everything is in place. The craft is shown by what's been left out as much as by what's there. The system is restrained in chrome and committed in meaning. Surfaces are flat. Type sets cleanly with weight contrast instead of decoration. Motion is quiet. The eight tag-type colors are the system's single permitted indulgence: a deliberate full palette that exists to encode taxonomy, never to decorate.
keyCharacteristics: Dark surface by default; light theme is a first-class peer, not an afterthought.
One warm accent (Ember Sunset) on ≤10% of any screen — the lamp in the workshop.
Tag spectrum (8 hues) carries semantic meaning, never decoration.
Flat-by-default surfaces with tonal layering (bg → surface → surface-elevated).
Sans-serif system stack: weight + scale contrast does the hierarchy work.
Bilingual EN/ES with parity in tone, length, and accessibility.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Lamp Ember is the only accent on the site. It appears on ≤10% of any screen and never as decoration — only on interactive affordances (CTAs, focus rings, link hover, active filter states) and on the single moments where the eye needs to be directed (Hero ambient bloom, impact callout dot). If a screen feels orange-heavy, the lamp is in too many places.

rules.name: The Spectrum Is Semantic Rule
rules.body: The eight tag-type colors are reserved for tag chips and tag-type labels. They do not appear on buttons, backgrounds, dividers, illustrations, or marketing copy. A coloured shape on this site means 'this belongs to a taxonomy type' — nothing else.

rules.name: The Neighbour Hazard
rules.body: Persimmon (tag-concepts) is the closest hue to Lamp Ember. Never place a concepts chip directly adjacent to a primary button or accented link: the affordance loses its singularity. Keep at least 24px of clear space, or move the chip into a different cluster.

rules.name: The No-Custom-Font Rule
rules.body: This site ships zero @font-face declarations. The system stack is the design choice, not a fallback. Anyone proposing a custom face must justify the perf and CLS cost against the principle that craft includes how fast the page loads.

rules.name: The Tight Tracking Rule
rules.body: Headings get negative tracking (-0.02em to -0.005em, larger sizes get more negative). Labels get heavy positive tracking (+0.25em) and UPPERCASE. Body stays at normal. This three-band tracking system gives the system its quiet confidence — nothing is set 'default'.

rules.name: The No Em Dash Rule
rules.body: Never use em dashes (—) or -- in any copy. Use commas, colons, semicolons, periods, or parentheses. Already enforced across the codebase; do not re-introduce.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. If a component looks like it needs a shadow to feel separate, the answer is wrong — use a border, tonal lift, or layout spacing instead.

rules.name: The State-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow on this site means 'you are about to interact with this'. It is a response, not a decoration. No drop shadows on logos, illustrations, headings, modals, or hero elements at rest.

rules.name: The Tonal Lift Rule
rules.body: Three tonal steps cover almost every elevation case: page (bg), resting surface (surface), and active/hover surface (surface-elevated). Reach for a shadow only when those three aren't enough; almost never.

dos: Do keep Lamp Ember to ≤10% of any screen. It is the lamp; rarity is the point.
Do treat the three-step tonal scale (bg → surface → surface-elevated) as the default elevation tool. Reach for a shadow only as a state response.
Do drive hierarchy through scale + weight (≥1.25 ratio between steps), tracking, and color contrast — never through ornament.
Do localize every visible string through useTranslations / getTranslator. Both EN and ES are first-class.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion. Every motion primitive in this codebase already does; new ones must.
Do keep focus rings visible at 2px in Lamp Ember with a 2px offset against bg. They are part of the craft, not a debug artifact.
Do ship the site fast. Static export, 0 client JS on Story/Deep-dive/Contact, system fonts, image decoding deferred. Performance is part of the message.
Do write copy as a senior engineer would — short sentences, specific verbs, concrete numbers, no hedging. The 'would a human actually say this?' test gates every line.
donts: Don't use Lamp Ember decoratively. Backgrounds, illustrations, dividers, headings: never. Only on interactive affordances and the singular eye-direction moments.
Don't use the tag-type colors anywhere outside tag chips and tag-type labels. The spectrum is semantic.
Don't place a Persimmon (tag-concepts) chip adjacent to a primary button or accented link. They share a hue and the affordance gets lost.
Don't introduce a custom @font-face without justifying the perf cost against the no-custom-font rule.
Don't use em dashes (—) or -- in copy. Commas, colons, semicolons, periods, parentheses.
Don't write LinkedIn-resume voice. 'Highly motivated data engineering professional…' fails the human-test instantly.
Don't try-hard developer brutalist. No monospace headings, no blinking cursors, no ASCII banners.
Don't agency-portfolio overdesign. No scroll-jacking, no oversized custom cursors, no decorative WebGL.
Don't ship a border-left/border-right greater than 1px as a colored stripe on cards or callouts.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text + gradient). Use a single solid color.
Don't decorate with glassmorphism. The scrolled navbar backdrop-blur-md is the one purposeful exception.
Don't build the hero-metric template (giant number + small label + supporting stats + gradient accent).
Don't ship a same-sized icon-and-heading-and-text card grid as the primary content.
Don't reach for a modal as the first thought. Exhaust inline and progressive alternatives.
